messages:
mira: quick thought — can we add a lightweight rollback signal to the console for config rollouts? thinking anomaly score + user-facing error spike threshold.
lee: +1. want something that doesn’t require a full eval run but still buys operators time.
anita: what exact metrics are we trusting? latency P99? error rate? quality regressions are harder.
mira: minimal set: p99 latency delta, 5xx rate, and a simple heuristic for user-facing latency > threshold. anomaly score = weighted sum.
jonathan: worried about noisy signals causing churn. need cooldowns and hysteresis.
casey: agree — also want a manual pause button and an auto-snooze that requires ops confirm before full rollback.
ops-bot: canary-deploy: rollout id r-2026-03-22-77 started to 5% cohorts.
lee: UX idea: show a single traffic-light with current status (green/yellow/red) and reason links to the telemetry that tripped it. clicking reason expands small charts.
manita?: (oops typo) anita: +1 for trace links. also add a "why" tooltip: exact rule that fired and the window.
mira: example rule — if p99 increases by >25% vs baseline AND 5xx rate increases >0.1% in 3m window => anomaly score > 0.6.
jonathan: baseline provenance? need to state whether baseline is rolling 1h median or deploy-time snapshot. we should default to rolling 1h median to avoid false positives on diurnal traffic.
casey: and tie cohort-level signals: allow per-tenant thresholds for big customers.
lee: for ops-runbook, we should emit a compact signal object on /internal/rollout_signals API: {"rollout_id","signal","score","reasons","snapshots_url"} — minimal fields so the runbook UI can call it.
mira: sounds good. prefer snake_case for the API. keep payload tiny.
jonathan: API auth? only console + oncall tokens. log to telemetry with rollout_id tag.
casey: also we need a "soft pause" vs "hard rollback" designation. soft pause reduces ramp to 0% but keeps canary alive for inspection. hard rollback reverts config.
anita: can we get a test harness? simulate signal generation in staging with synthetic traffic so console visualizations can be validated.
mira: plan: prototype signal calculator as a sidecar service that reads telemetry stream (metrics + error logs), publishes alerts to rollout_signals API, and console subscribes.
lee: rough timeline? prototype this week, basic console UI next sprint, staging test harness before EOD next week?
jonathan: add rate-limited notifications to oncall channel. no spam: only one alert per rollout per 15m unless severity increases.
casey: regarding thresholds, propose default conservative values, and an advanced panel to tweak per-flag thresholds (danger: people will over-tune).
anita: can we show historical rollback outcomes on the rollout page? like: rollout X triggered auto-pause, team inspected, resumed. helps build trust.
ops-bot: alert: rollout r-2026-03-22-77 anomaly_score=0.72 triggered at 1755554000 for cohort=eu-west-1.
lee: ok that’s the kind of real-world test we want. how does the console show reason? show top 2 contributing metrics with small sparklines.
mira: agree. small charts + link to logs and traces. also expose a quick "snapshot" export (JSON) for runbooks.
jonathan: edge-case: what if metrics source is delayed? fallback to 'unknown' and do not auto-rollback — only flag as yellow.
casey: ops request: a manual override TTL so if someone hard-rollbacks they can opt into suppressing auto-rollbacks for X minutes. must be auditable.
lee: audit trail: require operator + reason field. store in config_audit with tags.
anita: and tie this into the quality monitoring alerts so we can correlate model/regression evals with rollouts.
mira: action items: I’ll spin up a minimal signal calculator repo (proto) and add API spec. @lee will mock UI tiles. @jonathan will draft runbook notification rules. @casey will define pause vs rollback semantics for the API.
lee: I’ll throw a simple Figma mock and link it in the thread.
jonathan: recommend adding a "dry-run mode" for the signal calculator so we can observe without affecting rollouts.
casey: Can we do a quick CLI tool that queries /internal/rollout_signals for a given rollout_id? ops likes fast debugging.
manita?: (again typo) anita: CLI + small web endpoint to fetch snapshots. can do.
mira: thanks team. small ask: keep the first iteration conservative — default to notify + soft pause only. no auto-hard-rollback until we have 3 confirmed true positives.
lee: noted. thanks. :thumbsup:
console-bot: saved snapshot for r-2026-03-22-77 at 1755554600 (ui: rollback-signal-proto).
casey: leaving notes in the runbook doc about cooldowns and TTLs.
mira: closing loop: will open repo + PR by EOD and ping ops channel for staging validation.
jonathan: if anyone has quick objections to the conservative approach speak now, otherwise go ahead.
anita: no objections.
lee: no objections.
casey: no objections.
ops-bot: deploy-check: staging hook validated for rollout-signal-proto.
mira: thanks all — will post links when PRs are ready.
